text: Arizona lost 16–30 to Denver and fell to 2–5. The offense posted −0.11 EPA per play and the defense +0.20, and for the season the Cardinals are 19th in offensive EPA per play (−0.03) and 27th in defensive EPA per play allowed (+0.10). They are −66 on the season (142 for, 208 against), allow 29.7 points per game (32nd of 32), and have 8 takeaways against 6 giveaways.
DVOA has Arizona 23rd at −13.1%, down from 22nd (−10.8%) a week ago. The offense is 15th (−1.0%), the defense 29th (+14.1%) and special teams 11th (+2.0%).

Arizona has the 5th-most tight ends on the field (1.67 per snap) and one back on 87% of offensive plays (league 75%), with two or more backs on only 9% (league 19%). The defense plays fewer defensive backs than most (4.51 per snap, 28th of 32) and is worse against five or more rushers (+0.38 EPA on 30% of plays) than against four (+0.23 on 68%).

Arizona moves before the snap on 62% of plays (10th; league 58%), and the offense is worse with motion: −0.08 EPA per play against +0.03 without (25th vs 13th). Runs show it most, at −0.16 after motion and +0.14 without (2nd). The defense sees motion on 65% of plays (2nd) and is 16th against it (−0.02), but allows +0.32 without motion (32nd).

Arizona uses play action from under center on 14% of dropbacks (23rd; league 16%), and it adds value: +0.03 EPA per dropback with it against −0.03 without (20th vs 23rd), a +0.06 gain (15th). The defense sees play action from under center on 19% of dropbacks (5th most) and allows +0.30 (28th) against +0.26 without (31st).

Shotgun play action is barely in the plan: 4% of dropbacks (27th; league 7%), where it has produced +0.28 EPA (13th) against −0.03 without (23rd). Opponents use it on 6% of dropbacks against Arizona (22nd), and the defense allows +0.35 against it (25th) and +0.26 otherwise (31st).

Arizona is in heavy sets on 12% of plays (30th; league 21%), and they cost it: −0.14 EPA per play against −0.02 otherwise (28th vs 20th). Heavy-set runs average 2.8 yards (29th) at −0.25 EPA (28th), while heavy-set passes are +0.24 (12th). The defense faces heavy sets on 31% of plays, the most in the league, and holds them to −0.05 (14th) but allows +0.17 otherwise (30th).

Jacoby Brissett is 26th of 39 in EPA per dropback (−0.01 on 302), with 10 touchdowns, 6 interceptions and an 82.8 rating. He is quick to throw (2.63 seconds, 4th quickest of 37) and +5.4 in CPOE (5th), but his average target is 6.9 yards deep (33rd of 39, 1 = deepest). The offense is −0.25 EPA per dropback against the blitz and +0.08 without it.

Jeremiyah Love has 245 yards on 67 carries (3.7 per carry, rushing yards over expected of −0.39 per carry, 31st of 48), and Tyler Allgeier is at 2.9 per carry on 61 (−0.60 over expected, 39th of 48, −0.23 EPA). Bam Knight averages 6.4 per carry on 25 attempts for 160 yards, though at −0.09 EPA. The backs gain 2.1 yards before contact (28th), and Arizona's 22 broken tackles are tied for 9th.

Trey McBride still draws 29% of the targets, with 59 catches for 472 yards, 4 touchdowns and +0.24 EPA per target. Michael Wilson has 66 targets at −0.10 EPA each, and Kendrick Bourne is the efficient secondary option at +0.14 on 36 targets (25 catches, 234 yards). Elijah Higgins has 14 targets at +0.67 EPA each.

Pass protection is middle of the pack: Arizona was pressured on 22% of dropbacks (16th of 32), and its 5% sack rate ranks 10th. Hjalte Froholdt and Elijah Wilkinson have played every snap, Isaac Seumalo 99%, and Paris Johnson (55%), Jon Gaines (51%) and Jayden Williams (49%) rotate. The middle is still the leak: 71 runs up the middle average 2.6 yards at −0.21 EPA, while 20 left-end runs average 6.2.

The time of each sack isn't public, so FTN's charting is the best guide. Arizona allowed 15 sacks, up from 12 a week ago: FTN charts 5 when a standard rush won, 5 on extended plays, 3 against blitzes and 2 as quarterback-fault sacks. Brissett turned 22% of his pressures into sacks (15 of 68), against a 27% league rate.

The run defense is 10th in EPA per rush (−0.12), but the pass rush is thin: 6.9 pressures per game (29th of 32; league 9.0) and a 7% sack rate (14th) on 15 sacks. Budda Baker leads with 3.5 sacks and 5 QB hits, Darius Robinson has 2 sacks, 6 QB hits and 8 pressures, and Josh Sweat has 2 sacks and 8 pressures.

The pass defense is 31st in EPA per dropback allowed (+0.27). Budda Baker (27 targets, 257 yards, 3 touchdowns, 103.5 rating) and Denzel Burke (27 targets, 172 yards, 3 touchdowns, 102.7 rating) are the main problems, and Max Melton has allowed 84.4 on 25 targets. Andrew Wingard is the exception, with 8 targets, a 66.7 rating and an interception.

Arizona allows a 106.0 passer rating (28th of 32; league 91.5) and 8.2 yards per target (31st of 32), with 128 of 216 completed for 1,767 yards, 17 touchdowns (the most in the league) and 3 interceptions. Linebackers are the worst group at a 118.3 rating on 67 targets (31st), and edge and DL allow 134.4 (31st), while safeties (105.1, 19th) and cornerbacks (93.8, 18th) are closer to average.

Chad Ryland is 17 of 19 on field goals with a long of 60 and 13 of 13 on extra points, and special teams DVOA ranks 11th (+2.0%). Blake Gillikin averages 43.8 yards per punt and nets 37.6, with 9 of 33 punts inside the 20. Devin Duvernay (421 kick-return yards on 15 returns) and Jalen Brooks (499 on 19) carry the return game.

Atlanta beat San Francisco 29–20 to reach 3–4, its first win since Week 4, with no giveaways and four takeaways. The offense gained 298 yards at +0.05 EPA per play and the defense allowed 400 at +0.01, so the win came from the turnover margin more than from efficiency. Season offense has slipped to 25th in EPA per play (−0.05, from 22nd) and 26th per dropback (−0.10), though the run game is 8th per rush (+0.01). The defense is 14th in EPA per play allowed (−0.02), and the point differential has moved to −2 from −11.
DVOA moves Atlanta up to 19th overall (−0.5%, from 24th). The offense is 17th (from 20th), the defense 11th (from 15th), and special teams is still 30th (−5.4%).

Still run-leaning (PROE −6.3, 26th of 32) with 1.61 tight ends per snap (7th most). Two or more backs are on 21% of plays (league 19%) at +0.15 EPA per play, against −0.13 for one-back sets (72%). The defense rushes four on 74% of dropbacks (league 66%) and allows +0.08 EPA per play, against +0.10 for the league, and rushes five or more on 25% at −0.08.

Atlanta motions on 59% of plays (15th; league 58%). Pass EPA is −0.03 with motion (25th) against −0.18 without (29th), and passing yards per play are 6.8 with motion (11th) against 5.9 without (24th). On defense, Atlanta sees motion on 54% of plays (25th) and allows −0.07 EPA against it (7th), against +0.04 without it (20th).

Under-center play action is used on 17% of dropbacks (11th; league 16%) and has been the better call: −0.06 EPA with it (24th) against −0.15 without (29th), a +0.09 gain (13th; league +0.02). Opponents use it on 17% of dropbacks against Atlanta (14th) and gain +0.18 EPA (21st), against −0.05 on the rest (5th).

Shotgun play action is rare, 4% of dropbacks (28th; league 7%), but its 8 tries have produced +0.43 EPA (6th) against −0.15 without it (29th). Opponents have gained +0.68 EPA per dropback on shotgun play action against Atlanta (28th) on 15 tries.

Heavy sets (two or more backs besides the quarterback, or an extra eligible lineman) are 22% of Atlanta's plays (13th; league 21%) and produce +0.12 EPA per play (7th) against −0.10 in other sets (28th). Heavy runs average 4.8 yards (2nd; league 3.7), while the defense allows +0.04 EPA per play in heavy sets (23rd) against −0.03 otherwise (9th).

Michael Penix Jr. has 96 of 144 for 1,157 yards, 9 touchdowns, 1 interception and a 109.1 rating, with +0.14 EPA per dropback (13th of 39) and CPOE at +0.1 (21st of 37). He has the quickest time to throw in the league (2.53 seconds, 1st of 37), and Atlanta's dropbacks are +0.10 EPA with play action (n=49) against −0.14 without (n=178). The team's passing is −0.01 EPA per dropback against a blitz and −0.14 without one.

Bijan Robinson has 704 yards on 131 carries (5.4 per carry), +1.20 yards over Next Gen Stats' expectation per carry (4th of 48) and nine broken tackles on runs (PFR). Brian Robinson is the steadier change of pace at +0.05 EPA per carry (53 carries, 211 yards), while Bijan's receiving is still low value: 25 catches for 203 yards at −0.28 EPA per target on 32 targets.

Drake London is the passing game: 56 targets (29% share), 38 catches for 616 yards and +0.63 EPA per target, the best of the four with 15 or more targets, plus 1.6 yards after catch over expectation (14th of 125). He has his first touchdown after none through Week 6. Kyle Pitts has 4 touchdowns on 20 catches (+0.26 EPA per target), and Jahan Dotson has 2 on 12 catches from 25 targets at −0.26 EPA per target.

Pressure allowed is the league's lowest at 16% of dropbacks (1st of 32), and the line has 9 accepted penalties for 75 yards (4th fewest per game). Runs off the ends are the best plays: 8.7 yards per carry on 23 to the left end and 7.9 on 17 to the right (+0.41 EPA, the best lane), while middle runs average 3.1 yards at −0.23 EPA on 42 carries.

Of Atlanta's 16 sacks allowed, FTN charges 7 to blitzes (44%; league 26%), 4 to the quarterback, 4 to a standard rush and 1 to an extended play. Penix has turned 9 of 21 pressures into sacks (43%; league 27%), but with pressure allowed down to 16%, the leak looks like blitz pickup more than the line as a whole.

Atlanta's pass rush produces 11.1 pressures per game (tied for 3rd), but its 6% sack rate is 21st. Za'Darius Smith leads with 4.5 sacks and 5 QB hits in 105 snaps, Samson Ebukam has 2.5 sacks and 9 QB hits, and Cameron Thomas leads with 13 pressures and 11 QB hits. The run defense is 14th in EPA per rush (−0.09), and runs against light boxes are at −0.22 EPA per carry (league −0.07).

Pass defense is 12th in EPA per dropback allowed (+0.02). Jessie Bates III (5 TD on 26 targets, 111.4 rating) and Mike Hughes (4 TD, 130.1 rating on 40 targets) account for nine of Atlanta's 14 touchdowns allowed, while C.J. Henderson has held up (79.0 on 44 targets).

Atlanta allows a 96.4 passer rating in coverage (21st; league 91.5) and 64% completions (22nd). Safeties are the weak group at 117.4 (25th), corners are at 94.2 (20th), and linebackers are the strength at 82.9 (12th). Opponents have 14 touchdowns (tied for 25th, 1 = fewest) against 3 interceptions.

Special teams is 30th in DVOA (−5.4%) with 12 accepted penalties for 88 yards (29th). Nick Folk is 12 of 15 on field goals (long 51) and 15 of 16 on extra points, and Jake Bailey nets 40.2 yards per punt (computed) with 9 of 24 inside the 20.

4–3 after a 13–35 loss to Cincinnati, its second straight defeat, which cut the point differential from +24 to +2. The offense is 8th in EPA per play (+0.08, from 7th) and 9th in success rate (47%, from 6th), but it is averaging 24.1 points per game (12th, from 26.0). The defense fell from 11th to 17th in EPA per play allowed (+0.00), with the pass defense dropping from 9th to 17th (+0.05).

DVOA drops Baltimore from 8th to 15th (+4.7%) after the loss. The offense slipped from 6th to 10th (+6.8%), and the defense is still 17th but has moved from −1.8% to +1.8%. Special teams rose from 24th to 17th (−0.3%).

Baltimore has the 2nd most defensive backs on the field (5.14 per snap), and its offense plays the 6th most tight ends (1.64 per snap), so opponents see a light box (6 or fewer) on 59% of runs (league 44%). The defense sends five or more rushers on 31% of dropbacks (league 32%), and sending five or more (+0.02 EPA per dropback allowed) has held opponents slightly lower than the four-man rush (+0.06). On offense, one back on 72% of plays nets +0.11 EPA, against +0.04 from two or more backs.

Baltimore motions on 65% of offensive plays (6th; league 58%), and motion still lifts the run game: +0.05 EPA per run with motion (2nd) against −0.26 without (29th). Passing runs the other way, with +0.37 EPA on pass plays without motion (2nd) against +0.11 with it (14th), and 8.3 yards per pass play without motion (2nd) against 6.8 with it (12th). On defense, Baltimore allows −0.03 EPA against motion (14th) and +0.05 without (21st).

Baltimore uses play action from under center on 19% of dropbacks (6th; league 16%), for +0.19 EPA (13th) against +0.15 without (9th), a +0.04 gain (16th; league +0.02). Its success rate drops from 51% (4th) without play action to 46% (21st) with it. Opponents use it on just 11% of dropbacks against Baltimore (second-lowest share), and it has gone for −0.34 EPA (2nd) against +0.16 without (25th).

Shotgun play action is 7% of Baltimore's dropbacks (15th; league 7%), but it has been explosive on 16 plays: +0.79 EPA (3rd), 12.2 yards per play (3rd) and an 88% success rate (1st; league 46%), a +0.64 gain over dropbacks without it (2nd). On defense, opponents used it on 8% of dropbacks against Baltimore (5th most), and it has gone for −0.46 EPA (2nd) on 22 plays.

Baltimore lines up in heavy sets on 25% of plays (8th; league 21%), where it averages +0.08 EPA (10th), the same as its other sets (+0.08, 10th). The run is the efficient part: heavy-set runs average 4.6 yards per carry (4th; league 3.7) and +0.04 EPA (8th), while heavy-set passes are +0.16 (19th; league +0.15). Opponents line up heavy against Baltimore on 18% of plays (24th), and the defense has held those sets to −0.11 EPA (12th).

Tyler Huntley started again and went 23 of 34 for 298 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Cincinnati. For the season he has 106 attempts, 4 touchdowns, 1 interception and a 97.5 rating, along with −2.7 CPOE (30th of 37) and +0.05 EPA per dropback (21st of 39). His aggressiveness rate is 10.4% (33rd of 37, where 1 is highest) and his average depth of target is 6.3 (36th of 39, where 1 is deepest), while 42% of his pressures became sacks (6th of 42; league 27%). Lamar Jackson has not thrown since Week 4 (+0.38 EPA per dropback on 111 dropbacks) and has six carries for 40 yards (+0.48 EPA per carry).

Derrick Henry has 579 yards on 147 carries (3.9 per carry), with −0.14 EPA per carry, a 38% success rate and +0.05 rushing yards over expectation per attempt (22nd of 48). Justice Hill is again the efficient change of pace, with 140 yards on 21 carries (6.7 per carry, +0.17 EPA, 38% success). Baltimore's 15 broken tackles are tied for 20th most per game, and Henry has five on his runs (PFR, through Week 7).

Zay Flowers leads with 53 targets (27%), 608 yards and three touchdowns at +0.61 EPA per target, and he adds +3.2 yards of YAC over expectation (3rd of 125). Rashod Bateman is the most efficient target at +0.68 EPA on 26 targets (13%), while Mark Andrews has 37 targets (19%) at −0.10 EPA with three drops. Small-sample tight ends Josh Cuevas (+0.79 EPA on 11 targets) and Matthew Hibner (+1.34 on five) have been productive.

Baltimore allows pressure on 20% of dropbacks (9th of 32, where 1 is lowest) but has an 8% sack rate (24th), and Simpson (454 snaps), Rosengarten (452) and Ioane (403) have been the regulars, with Stanley on 83% of snaps. Left guard is the weak lane (−0.30 EPA on 27 carries, 2.2 yards per carry), while right end is the best (+0.14 EPA on 32 carries, 5.1 per carry). Baltimore's 19 accepted penalties for 131 yards rank 29th of 32 (where 1 is fewest per game).

No public stat times sacks, so pressure-to-sack rate and FTN's charting are the best guides. Huntley turned 42% of his pressures into sacks (league 27%; 10 sacks on 24 pressures), but FTN charged only three of Baltimore's 18 sacks to the quarterback (17%). Six came against blitzes (league 26%), five on extended plays (league 18%) and four on a standard rush (league 32%), which points at the protection and the play design more than at the quarterback.

Tavius Robinson leads with 3.5 sacks, eight QB hits and three tackles for loss on 64% of snaps, while Mike Green has three sacks and five TFL and Trey Hendrickson two sacks. Kyle Hamilton has seven tackles for loss and Trenton Simpson six. The pass rush lacks volume (8.1 pressures per game, tied for 21st; league 9.0), and the run defense is 18th in EPA per rush (−0.07).

Pass defense is 17th in EPA per dropback (+0.05), with Cincinnati's pass offense at +0.59 EPA in the game. Nate Wiggins has been the steadiest corner (36 targets, 220 yards, an 83.1 rating), while Marlon Humphrey has allowed 327 yards on 36 targets (102.4) and Malaki Starks two touchdowns on 17 targets (158.0). Kyle Hamilton has one interception on 28 targets, and Jaylinn Hawkins has a 125.5 rating on 18.

Baltimore allows a 97.1 passer rating (22nd of 32; league 91.5) on 148 of 229 passes (65%) for 1,762 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions, and 7.7 yards per target (19th; league 7.3). Linebackers are the strength (55.1, 1st of 32; league 91.5), while safeties (125.4, 27th; league 95.5) and corners (98.4, 27th; league 90.3) are the weak groups.

Tyler Loop is 12 of 15 on field goals with a 64-yarder and 17 of 17 on extra points. Ryan Eckley averages 47.1 yards per punt (42.0 net) with 13 inside the 20, and Chris Moore has eight kick returns for 229 yards. Special teams rose from 24th to 17th in DVOA (−0.3%), and the six accepted penalties (40 yards) are tied for 4th fewest per game.

Buffalo had a bye in Week 7 and stays 5–1. The offense is still 1st in EPA per play (+0.21) and leads the league in points per game (32.8), but the defense is 29th in EPA per play allowed (+0.13) and 30th in points allowed (28.5 per game). The turnover count is 9 giveaways against 6 takeaways, and the point differential is +26 (197 for, 171 against).

DVOA has Buffalo 4th overall at 21.7%, unchanged in rank through the bye. The offense is 2nd (+27.8%) and special teams 2nd (+6.5%), while the defense rose from 28th to 26th (+12.6%, lower is better).

Buffalo has the most tight ends per snap in the league (1.82) and the fewest running backs (0.99). Empty sets (12% of plays, +0.24 EPA) and one-back sets (65%, +0.24) are its best looks. On defense, four rushers allow +0.25 EPA (league +0.10) and five or more allow +0.26 (league +0.00), so neither rush count has worked.

Buffalo motions on 64% of snaps (7th; league 58%) and ranks 1st with motion (+0.20 EPA per play) and 3rd without it (+0.22), so motion barely changes the offense. The passing game is best without motion (8.9 yards per play, 1st) against 7.7 with it (2nd). On defense, motion makes little difference: +0.13 EPA allowed with it (29th) and +0.12 without (26th).

Buffalo calls play action from under center on 24% of dropbacks (3rd; league 16%) for +0.32 EPA (4th) and a 56% success rate (5th). Dropbacks without it are better (+0.34, 2nd), so the play-action gain is −0.02 (20th). Opponents use play action on 22% of dropbacks against Buffalo (1st) and average +0.30 EPA (27th).

Shotgun play action is rare for Buffalo (4% of dropbacks, 29th; league 7%), but its seven dropbacks have averaged +0.82 EPA (2nd) and 13.3 yards per play (2nd). Opponents have used it 12 times against Buffalo for +0.10 EPA (17th).

Buffalo is in heavy sets on 24% of plays (9th; league 21%), and they work: +0.10 EPA (9th) with a 53% success rate (2nd), though its other sets are better (+0.24, 1st). Heavy runs gain only 2.9 yards (28th) but +0.05 EPA (7th). Opponents use heavy sets on 27% of plays against Buffalo (3rd most) and average −0.03 EPA (15th), while other sets allow +0.19 (32nd).

Josh Allen has a 102.1 rating with 9 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, and ranks 3rd of 39 in EPA per dropback (+0.34). His completions are 2.4 points over expectation (14th of 37), but his 2.97-second time to throw ranks 30th of 37, where 1 is quickest, so he holds the ball longer than most. Pressure-to-sack is 32% (12 sacks on 38 pressures, 16th highest of 42; league 27%), and the offense's EPA per dropback is +0.33 with play action and without it, and +0.35 when blitzed against +0.32 when not.

James Cook has 627 yards on 117 carries (5.4 per carry, +0.05 EPA per carry) and is +0.93 yards per carry over expectation (7th of 48), with 8 broken tackles on runs. Buffalo is 1st in yards before contact per rush (3.3 against a league 2.5, including QB runs), and Ty Johnson has produced +1.35 EPA per target on 12 targets.

Keon Coleman is the most efficient of the four main targets at +1.00 EPA per target on 24 (19 catches, 283 yards, 3 touchdowns). Khalil Shakir leads in targets (32, a 20% share) with 22 catches for 290 yards and +0.31 EPA per target, while Dalton Kincaid has the most yards (315) and 1.9 yards of YAC over expectation (11th of 125). DJ Moore has 20 targets (12%) for 178 yards.

Dawkins, Torrence, McGovern and Anderson have played every snap, with Spencer Brown at 88%. Buffalo allows pressure on 19% of dropbacks (38 of 200, 6th lowest) and has a 6% sack rate (17th). Runs behind left guard have gained 5.0 yards at +0.39 EPA on 30 carries, runs at left end are the weak spot (−0.48 on 9), and the line has 13 accepted penalties for 100 yards (21st, where 1 is fewest).

Standard rush won 5 of Buffalo's 12 sacks allowed (42%; league 32%) and FTN charged 3 to Allen (25%; league 24%), so the blame splits. Allen turned 32% of pressures into sacks, 16th highest of 42 (league 27%), so the quarterback's share sits above average even with a low pressure rate allowed.

Gregory Rousseau has 6 of Buffalo's 11 sacks, 19 QB hits, 25 pressures and 8 tackles for loss, and Bradley Chubb has 1.5 sacks and seven QB hits. Pressure volume is strong (10.8 per game, 7th of 32; league 9.0), but the defensive sack rate of 4% ranks 26th (1 is highest), so pressures are not turning into sacks. The run defense allows −0.06 EPA per rush (22nd, where 1 is lowest), down from 20th last week.

The pass defense is 29th in EPA per dropback (+0.24). Christian Benford has allowed a 106.6 rating and 3 touchdowns on 36 targets, and Maxwell Hairston 99.8 with 2 on 22. Davison Igbinosun (91.7, 2 touchdowns on 31) and C.J. Gardner-Johnson (93.0, one interception on 21) have been the best regulars. The defensive backs have 17 accepted penalties for 157 yards (32nd, where 1 is fewest), and Buffalo gives up 3.5 first downs per game by penalty (32nd).

Buffalo allows a 102.4 passer rating in coverage (26th of 32; league 91.5), with 156 of 244 for 1,856 yards, 15 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Cornerbacks see 48% of targets and allow 97.1 (25th), safeties 109.1 (22nd) and linebackers 103.9 (26th).

Tyler Bass is 13 of 13 on field goals (long 49) and 18 of 20 on extra points. Greg Dortch averages 26.0 yards on 18 kick returns and Ray Davis 31.0 on 10, and Tommy Doman Jr. nets 46.0 yards on 12 punts with six inside the 20. Special teams rank 2nd in DVOA (+6.5%).

Carolina lost 13–43 to Tampa Bay at home, falling to 3–3 and cutting its point differential to −7 from +23. The offense gained 266 yards at −0.27 EPA per play with four giveaways and no takeaways, while the defense allowed 325 yards at +0.21. Season offense has slipped to 9th in EPA per play (+0.07, from 6th) and 6th in points per game (26.5), but the defense has slipped to 19th in EPA per play allowed (+0.02) and 30th against the run (+0.01 per rush). The turnover margin has swung from +3 to −1 (8 giveaways, 7 takeaways).
DVOA drops Carolina to 13th overall (+7.0%, from 7th), with the offense 12th (from 8th), the defense 15th (from 18th) and special teams 10th (+2.1%, from 3rd).

A pass-first offense (PROE +9.6, 1st of 32) with 2.43 receivers and 1.54 tight ends per snap (16th and 8th). Empty backfields (8%, 33 plays) produce +0.38 EPA per play against +0.13 for the league, while two-back sets have fallen to 9% (league 19%) at +0.31. On defense, Carolina plays 4.83 defensive backs per snap (7th most) and sends five or more on 37% of dropbacks, allowing −0.08 EPA per dropback against +0.10 on four rushers (61%).

Carolina motions on 56% of plays (18th; league 58%) and is 4th in EPA per play with motion (+0.14) against 21st without (−0.03). Dropbacks with motion gain +0.20 EPA (5th) against +0.02 without (17th), and runs gain +0.04 (4th) against −0.12 without (25th). The defense is 24th against motion (+0.06 EPA allowed) and 11th without it (−0.02), with opponents motioning on 53% of plays (27th).

Under-center play action is 14% of dropbacks (19th; league 16%) and works: +0.23 EPA with it (8th) against +0.12 without (10th), a +0.12 gain (9th). The defense holds opponents to −0.16 EPA on their under-center play action (7th), though opponents use it on only 13% of dropbacks (27th).

Carolina has the 3rd most shotgun play action (11% of dropbacks, league 7%), but it has been a drag: −0.13 EPA with it (22nd) against +0.12 without (10th), a −0.25 gain (26th). Opponents use it on 7% of dropbacks against Carolina (12th) and gain +0.27 EPA (22nd).

Heavy sets are only 10% of Carolina's plays (32nd, the lowest share; league 21%), but they are its best look: +0.29 EPA per play (1st) against +0.04 otherwise (13th), with heavy runs at +0.26 (2nd) on 24 carries. The defense has been strong against them at −0.18 EPA per play (7th), against +0.06 in other sets (25th).

Bryce Young's season line is 135 of 228 for 1,712 yards, 12 touchdowns and 4 interceptions (92.9 rating), with +0.10 EPA per dropback (18th of 39, from 8th), CPOE at +0.5 (20th of 37) and a 2.88-second time to throw (22nd of 37). His dropbacks are +0.16 EPA without a blitz and −0.01 against one.

Chuba Hubbard has 459 yards on 96 carries (4.8 per carry), +0.92 yards over Next Gen Stats' expectation per carry (8th of 48) and +0.10 EPA per carry, with 10 broken tackles on runs (PFR). He also caught 15 of 18 targets for 112 yards, 2 touchdowns and +0.58 EPA per target, the best of the six with 15 or more targets. The backups have not helped: AJ Dillon averages 2.5 yards on 17 carries (−0.56 EPA) and Jonathon Brooks 3.3 on 9.

Tetairoa McMillan is the target leader (54 targets, 26% share) with 36 catches for 511 yards, 2 touchdowns and +0.43 EPA per target, though his yards after catch sit 94th of 125 (YAC+ −0.3). Jalen Coker has 39 targets, 25 catches for 328 yards and 2 touchdowns (+0.22 EPA per target), and Darren Waller has 3 touchdowns on 14 catches (+0.41 per target) with Tommy Tremble at 16 catches for 136 yards and 2 touchdowns.

Pressure is the big problem: 30% of dropbacks pressured (76 of 256), the highest rate in the league (32nd), though the sack rate is 7% (20th). Walker, Hunt and Fortner have played 99%, 98% and 95% of snaps, and the line has 16 accepted penalties for 101 yards (tied for 27th). Runs behind left tackle average 7.0 yards at +0.24 EPA, while middle runs average 3.1 yards at −0.14 EPA on 35 carries.

Carolina's 17 sacks allowed are mostly on standard four-man rushes (10 of 17, 59%; league 32%) and extended plays (5, 29%), and FTN charges none to Bryce Young. His pressure-to-sack rate is 22% (17 of 76 pressures; league 27%), so he is pressured often but sacked less than the typical quarterback, which still points at the line more than at him.

Pressure is still high at 9.8 per game (10th), but the defense's 5% sack rate is 23rd, with 11 sacks in total.
